# Relift — Free Open-Source Data Recovery Tool

## Summary
Relift recovers deleted files from HDDs, SSDs, USB drives, SD cards, and disk images. It uses filesystem metadata (NTFS $MFT, FAT directories, ext4 inodes, APFS B-trees) to restore original names and paths, and falls back to validating signature carving for formatted or corrupted volumes. Strictly read-only on source, recovery only to a different physical volume.

## Install
- Windows: `winget install relift.vestige` or `scoop install relift`
- macOS: `brew install relift`
- Linux: `curl -sSL https://relift.rs/install.sh | sh` or `cargo install relift-cli`
- Docker: `docker run --privileged ghcr.io/shahabahmed01/relift scan /dev/sdX --session /data/session`

## Key capabilities
- Filesystem metadata undelete: NTFS, FAT12/16/32, exFAT, ext2/3/4, APFS, HFS+, Btrfs, XFS
- Validating file carving: 25+ formats (JPEG, PNG, PDF, ZIP/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX, MP4, MP3, SQLite, etc.)
- Disk imaging (ddrescue-style with mapfile)
- Session-based workflow with pause/resume
- SHA-256 verification of every recovered file
- Read-only guarantee (enforced at type level)
- CLI with JSON output, stable exit codes, shell completions
- GUI (Tauri 2 + Svelte 5): 3-screen flow, live results, preview, safe destination picker
- Cross-platform: Windows, macOS, Linux (x64 + ARM64)

## Limitations
- SSD with TRIM: content usually unrecoverable (controller erases blocks)
- Full format / secure erase / overwrite: data gone
- Encryption without key: impossible
- RAID 5/6 reconstruction: not yet implemented
- ext4 metadata undelete limited (extent tree zeroed on delete)
